title: Dynamic queue rebalancer & intake classifier for enterprise access requests
creator: Anita Chen
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers submit a steady stream of admin & access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML integrations, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). Our current intake is sticky and manual — requests pile on a single queue and require heavy PM/SE intervention to route and prioritize. This leads to SLA misses, inconsistent adjudication, and repeated context-switching for engineering and support.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New classifier tags incoming access requests with: type (RBAC|SSO|SCIM|Policy), risk score (0-100), and suggested SLA routing (Standard|Expedite|Legal). 2) Dynamic queue rebalancer moves tickets into workload buckets to maintain target SLA distribution: 90% Standard <72h, 95% Expedite <24h. 3) Admin console shows per-bucket backlog and estimated resolution time; PM/Support can override routing. 4) Metrics emitted to observability (latency, reassign rate, false positive rate) and documented in the runbook.
scope: Build a lightweight ML+rules classifier (first pass: heuristic feature set) + queue rebalancer orchestration. Integrations: Linear webhook, internal intake form, Support Zendesk connector (via webhook), and Console routing UI. Minimal schema: request_text, customer_tier, effected_scope (org/tenant), attachments, requested_action.
out_of_scope: Full ML model training pipeline, multi-language NLU beyond English, replacing existing RBAC entitlement workflows. Deep audit log changes (audit logging will be read-only consumer for now).
success_metrics: - SLA compliance: Increase on-time resolution from 76% -> 92% within 8 weeks. - Mean time to first-assignment reduced by 40%. - Manual routing overrides under 8% of automatically routed tickets after 4 weeks. - False positive expedite referrals <5%.
risks_and_mitigations: 1) Misclassification of sensitive requests could create security risk — mitigation: conservative risk threshold, human-in-loop for high-risk tags. 2) Over-automation -> customer frustration — mitigation: visible routing reason & easy override path. 3) Data sovereignty: ensure no sensitive PII is sent to external ML services; first-phase uses internal heuristics only.
implementation_notes: Phased approach: Phase 1 (2 sprints) build rule-based classifier + queue rebalancer + console view. Phase 2 (3 sprints) add lightweight supervised model backed by labeled historical intake examples, A/B test against rules, then promote to canary. Use feature flags for rollout. Add observability hooks for latency, routing confidence, override count.
stakeholders: PM: Anita Chen; Eng: Jordan Patel (owner), Sofia Martinez (backend), Riz Ahmed (infra); Design: Priya Rao (UX); Support lead: Marco Li; Security reviewer: Elena Kovalenko.
